narrative.overview:
Money is drawn as a connected map. Cards are places, hairlines are the routes between them, and light travels those routes when money moves. The system exists to make one number trustworthy at a glance, what is safe to spend, by showing what feeds it. Everything outside the map stays deliberately ordinary: standard navigation, standard controls, sentence-case labels and plain rows, so the moving part keeps its meaning.

The world comes in two themes, Obsidian Gold and Midnight Emerald, each with a dark and a light mode, set by `data-theme` and `data-mode` on the root element. Every combination carries exactly one accent and one hero surface that stays dark and tinted even in light mode. Gold is the default world. Density is phone-first and calm: one clear thing per screen, with further detail behind a tap, a tab or a count. The light-mode grounds are recorded as built, and remain open to the owner's reaction.

The confirmed rejections are a rainbow palette, the dullness of a bank app, and a crowded single screen.
keyCharacteristics: A node map on Home, joined by live canvas lines, over conventional controls everywhere else.
One accent per theme, with status hues reserved for status.
Display numerals at one weight, with the rupee sign supplied by dedicated faces.
Soft rings and shallow ambient shadows rather than borders.
Motion that reports a real change: a comet travels, a card lifts, the number counts.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each theme has one accent. Good, warn and bad are status colors and do not count, so gold's green `good` is legitimate; a second decorative hue is not.

rules.name: The Hero Stays Dark Rule
rules.body: The hero surface is dark and tinted in every mode, and there is one on a screen.

rules.name: The One Hue Chart Rule
rules.body: Data is read by position and label. Charts use one hue and one neutral, and categories are never color-coded.

rules.name: The Rupee Face Rule
rules.body: Bodoni Moda, Hanken Grotesk and Sora do not contain the rupee sign (U+20B9). Self-hosted faces supply only that character through `unicode-range`: Noto Serif latin-ext beside Bodoni Moda, Mukta latin-ext beside Hanken Grotesk, and Mukta at `size-adjust: 118%` beside Sora. Any stack that can show an amount keeps its rupee face directly after the primary family, so the sign is never left to a system fallback.

rules.name: The Single Display Weight Rule
rules.body: Only weight 500 of Bodoni Moda ships. Display text always uses the `--display-weight` property, so the browser never synthesizes a bold serif.

rules.name: The Display For Figures Rule
rules.body: The display face belongs to figures, page titles and the brand. Section titles, labels, buttons and running text stay in the body face.

rules.name: The Ring Not Border Rule
rules.body: Cards, fields, chips and ghost buttons draw their edge with an inset shadow, so an edge never changes layout. The dashed goal route is the one true border, because it is a line and not an edge.

rules.name: The Earned Drop Rule
rules.body: A plain card has no drop shadow. Drops belong to map tiles, the Add button, sheets, toasts and the tab pill.

rules.name: The Comet Tells The Truth Rule
rules.body: A bright event comet runs only on a line that the changed value passed through. Only the faint resting light is ambient.

rules.name: The Lines Decorate Rule
rules.body: The canvas is hidden from assistive tech and ignores pointers. Every tile is an ordinary link, and the page must work fully without the lines.

rules.name: The Motion Falls Back Rule
rules.body: Under reduced motion, lines appear complete, comets and lifts are skipped, numbers update at once, and all CSS motion collapses. No information may exist only in motion.

dos: Do use the role custom properties, so a component works in all four combinations without a mode check.
Do check new surfaces in both themes and both modes; a gold-dark result does not prove the other three.
Do use `--ease`, `cubic-bezier(.23, 1, .32, 1)`, for movement, with press feedback at about 140ms and color changes at 160ms.
Do keep a rupee face in any font stack that can display an amount, and format figures with tabular lining numerals and Indian digit grouping.
Do keep Home led by the map, with supporting items behind a count or below it, and let detail pages use ordinary stat grids and connected cards.
Do run every new animation through the reduced-motion paths, in CSS and in script.
donts: Don't make the interface rainbow-coloured, dull like a bank app, or crowded on one screen.
Don't add a second accent hue or color-code categories; status colors stay reserved for status.
Don't put a second hero surface on a screen or lighten it in light mode.
Don't set Bodoni Moda at any weight other than 500.
Don't set body-face labels in uppercase or wide tracking; the build has neither.
Don't add map lines that connect things money does not move between.
Don't make a control depend on a canvas, hover or a comet to be understood.
